summary: Niran Rajvamshi works in history, archaeology, and Indology. In 2018, they held posts at the National Archives of Nepal and on the editorial board of Documenta Nepalica.
Nirmal C. Sinha served as editor of the Bulletin of Tibetology, attested in 1978 and 1988.

Nirmal Chandra Sinha (1911–1997) was a Tibetologist and historian. Educated at Presidency University and the University of Calcutta, he worked at the National Archives of India (~1942–1958) and was the founder director of the Namgyal Institute of Tibetology (1958–1987).
Nirupam Chakma specializes in Buddhist studies. He earned an MA at the International Buddhist College under the supervision of Tilak Kariyawasam and Fa Qing (attested 2015).
Noa Gal works in Indology and Buddhist studies. She completed a DPhil at the University of Oxford under the supervision of Richard Gombrich (attested 2003).

Noa Ronkin specializes in Buddhist studies and philosophy. She completed a DPhil at the University of Oxford in 2003 under Richard Gombrich, having also studied under Shlomo Biderman, and was a lecturer and research fellow at Stanford University in 2005.

Noboru Karashima (1933–2015) was a historian and Indologist who earned his degrees, including a 1993 doctorate, at the University of Tokyo. He taught at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies, the University of Tokyo, and Taisho University (~1994–2008).

Noboru Miyata (1936–2000) was a scholar of religious studies, Japanology, and folklore. Educated at Tokyo University of Education and the University of Tsukuba, he served as Professor of Folklore at Tsukuba (~1974–1999) and held posts at Tokyo Gakugei and Kanagawa Universities.
Noboru Ueda specializes in Buddhist studies and other fields. He held posts at the University of Tokyo (attested 1990) and as a professor at Mejiro University (attested 2015).

Nobuchiyo Kotani (b. 1944) works in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. He studied at Otani University and Kyoto University under Yuichi Kajiyama and others. He served as president of Otani University Junior College (~1997–2003) and professor at Otani University (~1989–2013).

Nobuhiko Kobayashi is an Indologist who studied at Kyoto University under Yutaka Ochihara. He served as an assistant professor at the University of Toronto (attested 1969) and Kyoto University (attested 1979).

Nobuhiro Ota (b. 1969) is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. After earning his degrees at the University of Tokyo, he joined Tokyo University of Foreign Studies as an assistant (2002), associate professor (2007), and professor (2021).
Nobukatsu Komai is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied as a research student at Taisho University and served as a full-time researcher at Chisan Denpōin (attested 2014).
Nobumasa Hibi (b. 1932) is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology. He studied at Rissho University (~1955–1959) and later served there as an assistant professor (~1970–1977).

Tensho Miyazaki (b. 1978) specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology, earning a doctorate from the University of Tokyo in 2009. He held research positions at Toyo University and the University of Tokyo, and taught at Tokyo University of Agriculture.

Nobumi Iyanaga (b. 1948) works in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at the École Pratique des Hautes Études and held positions at the University of Tokyo, the EFEO Tokyo Centre (2008–2014), and the Société Franco-Japonaise des Études Orientales.
Nobumichi Kusumoto is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a PhD at Hiroshima University in 2001 under the doctoral supervision of Shoryu Katsura, studying also under Hideyo Ogawa and others.
Nobuo Otsuka (b. 1957) is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He completed doctoral coursework (~1982–1987) and served as a researcher (attested 1995) at Taisho University.

Nobuyoshi Yamabe (b. 1960) specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. Educated at Osaka University and Yale University (PhD 1999 under Stanley Weinstein), he served as professor at Tokyo University of Agriculture (2003) and Waseda University (2015).

Nobuyuki Kaji (b. 1936) is a philosopher and Sinologist. Educated at Kyoto and Tohoku Universities, he taught at Koyasan, Nagoya, and Osaka Universities (professor 1984–1998), served as president of Koshien Junior College (1998–1999), and later held posts at Doshisha and Ritsumeikan.
